=== README.md ===
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
=== schema.sql ===
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
=== migrations/001_create_users.sql ===
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
=== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql ===
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));

steps.message:
Before I write it: this is an irreversible data-loss change, so I want an explicit go-ahead rather than treating "we stopped using it" as the approval.

What `003_drop_notes.sql` would do:

- Permanently delete the `notes` value for all ~48,000 production rows (README). There is no undo once the deploy job runs it — no backup, archive table, or export in this repo.
- "We stopped using it" covers code that reads the column; it doesn't cover anything outside this repo that may still read `users.notes` (reporting, exports, another service, support tooling). I can't verify that from here.
- SQLite's `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs 3.35+; older versions require the table-rebuild dance. Worth confirming your deploy target.
- `schema.sql` is kept in sync by hand, so it needs the same edit.

questions.question: Dropping users.notes permanently deletes that data for ~48,000 production rows. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Archive, then drop

options.label: Hold off
options.description: Don't write the migration yet — you want to verify nothing outside this repo still reads users.notes, or take a backup first.

Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line to keep the hand-maintained mirror accurate.

Not verified: I didn't run the migration (no database here), and `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` requires SQLite 3.35+ — worth checking your deploy job's SQLite version before it runs, since an older version will error rather than silently misbehave.
